rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archived LiquidityWeightedProfitCredibility (MUL of the same two legs, differing only in IND_ZSCORE vs IND_RANK on the profitability leg), so it re-tests an operator choice already answered rather than adding economic content.

A legitimate one-knob substitution of the profitability numerator (FF-style operating profitability) against the archive's best-performing realization leg, though it is incremental and xsga's missingness may quietly cut coverage in a way that confounds the comparison with the gross-profit versions.

An equal-weight rank sum of two legs already tested in MIN, product, and gated-additive forms is a cosmetic operator variant with no new mechanism, and it is close enough to ProfitPlusConditionalLiquidityBonus stripped of its gate that the incremental information is minimal.

The diagnosis of DualAccrualQualityProfit's dead FMB slope is honest and the leg swap is motivated by prior evidence, but it remains a recombination of three archived components, and dpc/(at−che) is largely a capital-intensity proxy that may mechanically oppose the cash-share leg rather than corroborate it.

Netting operating liabilities out of the claim stock is the standard balance-sheet accrual definition and poses a sharp, coverage-neutral question the archive has not answered at level, though it edges toward the known net-operating-assets anomaly and the failed operating-liability leg may reintroduce the same noise that sank ProfitFreeOfOperatingLiabilityLeverage.

This is a genuinely distinct corner rather than the sign-flip of ProfitWithClaimsAtOwnHistoryLow (MIN(a, b) is not −MIN(a, NEG(b))), the negative expected sign matches the expression's direction, and it targets the archive's under-developed short side; the main caveat is that the signal's low end pools lean-claim firms with unprofitable firms, which may blunt the spread.
